_about: Story state, reader-safe. Claude-owned. Update after every scene and climax. Never put real-world numbers here; GM-only state (plan, flags, factions, companions to come) lives in saga/state/_gm/plan.json and approval moves only through saga.py add. covers lists the days a scene drew on; whether a day is closed lives in the Ledger, not here. The site's Now page gives each field one job, so a fact belongs in one of them: last_beat is the latest scene or Between, current_quest.on_the_page the quest, current_struggle what he is fighting (a sentence or two), location.detail where he is (a phrase); a companion's line there is their character file's last_seen_doing. tether is projected from the records: the Tether stages the page has paid, each with the block that paid it (the Wardrobe opens its pieces for the two of them by it).

location.detail: a frozen stream running up into the forest from the Wend, a little north of where the company crossed
location._about: place is an id from saga/state/places.json; detail is a short phrase, where in the place he is (the site prints it after the place's name). Weather is season's, events are last_beat's

season: deep winter at the Wend: snow over the river ice, and old forest beyond it

current_quest.name: Over the River
current_quest.on_the_page: Over the frozen Wend and in under the trees of the Thornwild, the clans' country, with what the stones say and the grey cloaks' smoke behind him on the causeway. He wants a roof among people who have every reason to refuse him one, and the truth of the ford from the far side of it.
current_quest._about: on_the_page is what the site shows and must be supported by the chronicle; the GM's own summary lives in saga/state/_gm/plan.json (quest_summary). One job: the quest itself (who wants what, what stands in the way, the price), not the latest scene (last_beat) or what he is fighting (current_struggle)

current_struggle: The forest across the river, and whatever it is full of.
last_beat: Rae walked the cart up onto the frozen stream into the forest by her grandmother's way, and Darrow came last, with the cold lamp behind them and its black chip turning on its thong in no wind at all.

maelis.note: has told him what she dared, and not where she learned it; the Confessor's eyes found her at the gate; she approved his name at the bars in her own coin

hollis.note: second on the list, read at the bars; dry, and has told Darrow so; saw him move at his name, and called him Captain when he gave it

wren.note: afraid; hides it with numbers; ran for the bell on his word; made him promise to tell her first next time

rae.note: the carter of the last cart; came up the Steps with his letter in her shirt and calls him Darrow, not Ser, not Captain; her stake sits beside his on NOBODY in the kitchen's book, and he owes her an aye; goes down to her oxen at the winch-house and comes up when she is owing

ash.note: the grey hound from the kennels; eats only from his left hand; came off the bars to her name and sleeps under his cot

choices.text: Tell the lay brothers the Faithless went down the far side a week ago. Let the valley carry it.
Step forward and answer to his name.
Ask Maelis to take him down herself, on her terms: her count, a hand on Wren's shoulder, her right to say stop.
Write back as a brother: he will not kneel, and why
Send down his name as surety: a captain's word, though the Faithless have no credit in the Lowmarch.
Tell Hollis and the far cots' keepers first, and the Prior only after: his own people before the House's law.
Use him: his next letter down carries what the Captain wants the Confessor to believe.
His own: go down to the lower terrace at dawn and take the Confessor's attention onto himself, without telling him what the script showed.
Let Rae answer for her own cart.
His own: told him he knelt the morning of the ford and the warmth went out of him halfway across the river, and bought him a drink.
North by the mill tracks, the safe road for his own.
His own: told Rae it was her ox and her call, and the company would stand behind whatever she decided
Answer by the forms: go to the weir at the hour named, alone, and let the company watch from the bank.

His own: let her up with a message for the man who sent her, in his own words: enough of the ford as he saw it from the water that whoever sent her will know he knows, and nothing that tells them which road the company takes or how much he has. Then watch her walk to her horse.

His own: he says why first, out loud, to all four at the fire: the forty need the company, and they are to put distance between themselves and the walkers; he goes west on the trail at first light with Ash, two nights out, to find how the walkers can be stopped, and will catch the company up. He asks nobody to come.

His own: gave her the old answer about the Steps, owned it was not the reason, and told her the rest: what the rider said on the ice, the cold he has seen beside the stones, and what Maelis made of him that a stone would take back. It wasn't his. This is.
All of it, at once, before Hollis has finished asking: the three heartbeats, the Second dry on its bank, the horse already turned when the order came.
Tell the company, all of it, here at the ring, with Maelis's one word behind him.

inventory: the summons under the forms, taken down nail by nail, inside his coat
a drover's coat, brown wool, caped at the shoulders, the fork-hole in the cape mended and a fresh cut across the cape at the shoulder
the borrowed stick, used on the Steps and kept
Elinor's letter, from the miller, opened, inside his coat
Aldric's last letter, the small sheet (*Answer me, or I will come myself*), inside his coat

keepsakes.name: A name said once
keepsakes.text: The word Quickstep, said of him once as a jeer by the youngest of the Ninth in a fair's yard; he walked on as though he had not heard it, and it stayed in the yard when the Ninth rode out.

keepsakes.name: The ox-bell
keepsakes.text: Her grandmother's plain dark ox-bell, warm from her hip, tied to Rae's own belt at the Coldmere bell-house.

recaps._about: One-line 'previously' per chapter file slug, shown at the top of that chapter in the reader. Spoiler-free; only what earlier chapters showed.
recaps.01-the-confessor-at-the-steps: At Harrow Ford the Grace went out of the Ninth Lance in mid-river, and only a thread of it came back; Darrow's knee gave way with no blade near it, and forty-one of his sixty did not come home. Carried up the Thousand Steps to Saint Ysolde's, he chose Maelis Vorne's Binding over kneeling again at the Oathspire.
recaps.02-the-grey-cot: The House was frightened, the Confessor had given it a word, and a lad lay Hollowed in the Grey Cot with frost on his mouth; Darrow, with Wren for his legs, went looking for whoever had passed in the night, and found that nobody had.
recaps.03-the-undercroft: Under the House, in a hall older than it, Darrow found what makes the stone grow frost: a black sliver shut in the wall beneath the row with a lid of new mortar, carried up the Steps in the House's own letter-satchel. It would not come out of the rock; the cold whitened his fingers before he let it go on the Mender's word, and it stays. Now the whole House has seen them come up, and he must decide who is told.
recaps.04-old-mercy: Old Mercy: the rope cut, the stair held from a chair, the bell rung on the last of the light, and the Thousand Steps walked down at last.
recaps.05-the-thornwild-woman-s: The list is read again at Coldmere's bell, and the company hears it from across the water; the carter who brought him home pays for the hiding in her own book, and the road out is his to choose.
recaps.06-the-weir: At the noon bell on the frozen weir, the rider's footwork met a man who would not move; she lies on the ice, and the choice is his.
recaps.07-the-far-bank: At the ring in the frozen marsh Darrow read what the stones are for, Wren read the line he could not, and Maelis said yes.
